## Declarations and implementations

```plato

    // The matrix that mirrors points through the plane:
    // p' = p - 2 (Dot(N, p) - Distance) N. In row-vector form the linear block is
    // I - 2 N (x) N (symmetric, so transposition is moot) and the translation row
    // is 2 Distance N. The plane is normalized first so a broken unit invariant
    // cannot scale the reflection.
    CreateReflection(_: Matrix4x4, value: Plane): Matrix4x4
    {
        var p = value.Normalize;
        var n = p.Normal.Vector;
        var d = p.Distance;
        return (Number4(1.0 - 2.0 * n.X * n.X, 0.0 - 2.0 * n.X * n.Y, 0.0 - 2.0 * n.X * n.Z, 0.0),
                Number4(0.0 - 2.0 * n.Y * n.X, 1.0 - 2.0 * n.Y * n.Y, 0.0 - 2.0 * n.Y * n.Z, 0.0),
                Number4(0.0 - 2.0 * n.Z * n.X, 0.0 - 2.0 * n.Z * n.Y, 1.0 - 2.0 * n.Z * n.Z, 0.0),
                Number4(2.0 * d * n.X, 2.0 * d * n.Y, 2.0 * d * n.Z, 1.0));
    }

    // The matrix that flattens points onto the plane along `lightDirection`,
    // turning geometry into its own shadow. The projection of p is p - s L with
    // s = (Dot(N, p) - Distance) / Dot(N, L); the matrix carries that expression
    // multiplied through by Dot(N, L), leaving the divide to the homogeneous w
    // component (w' = Dot(N, L)). Row-vector form, so column j of row i is the
    // i-th component's contribution. Degenerate when the light runs parallel to
    // the plane (Dot(N, L) = 0), where the shadow is not defined.
    CreateShadow(_: Matrix4x4, lightDirection: Vector3D, plane: Plane): Matrix4x4
    {
        var p = plane.Normalize;
        var n = p.Normal.Vector;
        var l = lightDirection;
        var k = n.Dot(l);
        var d = p.Distance;
        return (Number4(k - n.X * l.X, 0.0 - n.X * l.Y, 0.0 - n.X * l.Z, 0.0),
                Number4(0.0 - n.Y * l.X, k - n.Y * l.Y, 0.0 - n.Y * l.Z, 0.0),
                Number4(0.0 - n.Z * l.X, 0.0 - n.Z * l.Y, k - n.Z * l.Z, 0.0),
                Number4(d * l.X, d * l.Y, d * l.Z, k));
    }

    // The IHashable obligation Plane inherits through IGeometry -> IValue. Both
    // fields participate in the digest, following the VertexPair / Chromaticity
    // pattern; the compiler does not derive Hash.
    Hash(pl: Plane): Integer
        => pl.Normal.Vector.Hash * 31 + pl.Distance.Hash;

    //==
    // # Slabs
    //
    // A slab is the preimage of a closed number interval under the linear map
    // p -> Dot(Normal, p), so containment is exactly interval containment.
    // `Contains(IInterval, value)` (P4) is endpoint-inclusive and assumes the
    // interval is stored forward (Start <= End), which is the slab's own invariant.

    // True when the point's signed distance along Normal lies within Interval.
    Contains(s: Slab2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => s.Interval.Contains(point.PositionVector.Dot(s.Normal.Vector));

    // True when the point's signed distance along Normal lies within Interval.
    Contains(s: Slab3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => s.Interval.Contains(point.PositionVector.Dot(s.Normal.Vector));

    // The three axis-aligned slabs of a box, one per world axis (X, Y, Z), each
    // spanning that axis' Min..Max coordinate. A point lies in the box exactly when
    // it lies in all three slabs, which is the standard slab reduction of a
    // ray/box or box/box test.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slab_method
    Slabs(b: Bounds3D): Array<Slab3D>
        => [Slab3D(Direction3D(Vector3D.UnitX), NumberInterval(b.Min.X, b.Max.X)),
            Slab3D(Direction3D(Vector3D.UnitY), NumberInterval(b.Min.Y, b.Max.Y)),
            Slab3D(Direction3D(Vector3D.UnitZ), NumberInterval(b.Min.Z, b.Max.Z))];
}
```
